title: Top Democrat gives a statement about Stephen A. Smith's rumors Presidential offer in 2028
text:
By Oliver Salt
Published: 21:45 GMT, February 13, 2025 | Updated: 21:47 GMT, February 13, 2025
Huisminheid leader Hakeem Jeffries admits that ‘a lot can be found’ about Stephen A. Smith in the midst of the ESPN -Gastheer who Rent for President in 2028.
A recent poll showed that Smith, who has become the face of ESPN over the past decade, would get more support than a number of large democratic presidential hopeful democrat when the next elections arrive.
And during an exclusive interview with DailyMail.com last week, he hinted on a possible presidential bid in three years after his conviction that he would “defeat every candidate about that poll.”
“If they told me that I had a legitimate, bona fide shot to win the presidency of the United States of America, I would entertain it,” Smith said.
‘Because the part I don’t joke about is that I believe that I could beat every candidate on that poll. Every candidate they called them, from Kamala Harris directly to (Pete) buttigieg and to Tim Walz. I would beat them all. I believe that. I really do it. ‘
And while calling for Smith to consider walking, the pace of collecting, top democrat Jeffries was interviewed about the prospect that the sports analyst came up as a serious candidate for 2028.
Top Democrat Hakeem Jeffries admits that ‘a lot can be found’ about Stephen A. Smith (photo)
Jeffries was questioned about talking about the ESPN personality that is for president in the 2028 elections
He first emphasized that the next elections is ‘far away in the distance’ and not a current priority before he adds: “There is a lot to be found in Stephen A. Smith.”
Smith was not removed from delivering daring political views on the aftermath of the emphatic victory of Donald Trump in Kamala Harris in the polls last November.
As a result of his Hot Takes, the media personality has generated a lot of support for a potential presidential bid.
He recently shocked Bill Maher’s audience with his blunt judgment about why Trump won a second term in the White House – and admitted why he feels a ‘damn fool’ for supporting Harris.
Although he played the prospect, Smith also opened the door for a possible presidential run when he spoke with DailyMail.com on Super Bowl Week in New Orleans.
The 57-year-old said: ‘You know, instead of talking about the fact that I am an elected officer or a runner for the President of the United States, what about I am someone with a voice that is as strong as Those of Sean Hannity, as strong as Mark Levin’s, as strong as Rachel Maddow. What about that?
“Because that is more likely. However, I will admit, as I said, I don’t feel like doing this, but going out looked at me and said, “Yo, man, we want you to run to the office,” and I had a legitimate shot for it To win presidency of the United States, I am not going to lie. I will think about that.
“But I have to have my money. I’m not going to the White House broke. I’m not going to do that. I have to have my money. I have to have my home. I have to have my financial situation fully taken care of. I am not worried if that happens for me. ‘
Smith told DailyMail.com exclusively that he might consider running for president
Smith’s comments came after John McLaughlin – who was the most important poller of Trump – had a national investigation of 1,000 general election voters last month.
One of the questions he asked was: “Thinking ahead of the 2028 democratic primary elections for President, if those elections were held today among the following candidates, for whom would you vote?”
Two percent said they would choose Smith. That is more than Beto O’Rourke – who ran for the nomination in 2020 – and JB Pritzker, the governor of Illinois (both a percent).
It is remarkable that Smith has only questioned one percentage point behind Tim Walz – Vice -Presidential Pick by Harris – and Pennsylvania – Governor Josh Shapiro.
Harris was overwhelming the No. 1 choice, with a third of voters (33 percent) and said they would vote for the former Vice President – despite her defeat by Trump in November.
